title: Best Steam Irons UK
short: Steam irons compared for crease-busting power, glide and hard water handling, from budget lightweight models to premium steam generators.
intro: A steam iron's real test is how it copes with a genuine ironing pile, not just its spec sheet. This guide compares irons hand-tested by Mumsnet's testers in their own homes over months, tackling school uniforms, bedding and delicate fabrics while assessing steam output, soleplate glide and hard water performance.

products.name: 20630 Powersteam Ultra Steam Iron
products.best_for: Buyers who want reliable, powerful ironing without paying a premium
products.key_spec: 70g/min continuous steam, 210g steam shot, 350ml tank, ceramic soleplate
products.summary: Mumsnet's Laura found no fancy gimmicks here, just a high-performance, powerful steam iron at an affordable price, with chunky trigger buttons and an easy-pour water jug making it really user-friendly. It tackled the most stubborn creases with ease and held its own against pricier rivals in testing, though it's heavier than lightweight alternatives.

products.name: LightGlide Steam Iron
products.best_for: Occasional ironers or anyone who wants the lightest possible iron
products.key_spec: 924g (lightest tested), 24g/min continuous steam, 230ml tank, no auto shut-off
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Alison found this the lightest iron tested at just under 1kg, making ironing feel less of a chore and particularly good for anyone with mobility issues like arthritis. It glides easily across fabrics with a respectable 100g steam shot, though it's not as powerful as pricier options and lacks an automatic shut-off.
pros: Lightest iron tested, easy to manoeuvre
cons: Not as powerful as pricier irons

products.name: Vaporella Quick Q100
products.best_for: Buyers in hard water areas who don't want scale build-up hassle
products.key_spec: 40g/min continuous steam, 250g steam shot, indicator light for descaling, works with plain tap water
products.summary: Mumsnet's editor Poppy O'Neill found this properly shifts creases on everyday laundry without endless re-going-over, and crucially doesn't require filtered or distilled water even in hard water areas. A self-clean indicator light and calc clean setting take the guesswork out of maintenance, though there's no 'ready' light or fabric labels on the dial.
pros: Indicator light warns when descaling is needed
Works with plain tap water, even in hard water areas
cons: No fabric labels on the temperature dial

products.name: Azur 8000 Series Steam Iron
products.best_for: Buyers who want steam-generator-rivalling power without the bulky tank
products.key_spec: 85g/min continuous steam, 260g steam shot, single temperature technology, 1-minute heat-up
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Alison found this heats up in just one minute, much quicker than other irons, and glides easily through creases with steam rivalling a steam generator. Single temperature technology means no adjusting between fabrics, automatically protecting delicates from overheating, though it's nearly 2kg and one of the priciest conventional irons around.
pros: Powerful steam output rivalling steam generators

products.name: Freemove Power Cordless Steam Iron
products.best_for: Buyers who want the freedom of a cordless iron without long charging waits
products.key_spec: 30-second heat-up, 12-second recharge, 35g/min continuous steam, 200g steam shot
products.summary: Mumsnet's Poppy O'Neill found this the best cordless design tested, with a speedy 12-second recharge that felt convenient and didn't prolong ironing sessions. It's more powerful than several corded rivals with a whopping 200g steam shot, and thoughtful touches like a horizontal charging base and safety catch make it a pleasure to use, though the water tank is on the smaller side.
pros: Very fast heat-up and recharge times
Powerful steam shot for a cordless design
Horizontal charging base and safety lock
cons: Smaller water tank than corded rivals

products.name: PerfectCare Compact Steam Generator Iron
products.best_for: Buyers ready to invest in professional-level ironing speed
products.key_spec: 120g/min continuous steam, 400g/min steam shot, 1.5L tank, OptimalTEMP single-temperature technology

Compact enough to fit a standard ironing board
One temperature setting suits all fabrics safely

guide.q: Standard iron, cordless or steam generator: which should I choose?
guide.a: A standard steam iron like the Russell Hobbs here covers most needs affordably. A cordless model like the Tefal Freemove suits anyone who finds a trailing cable annoying, recharging in seconds between sections. A steam generator like the Philips PerfectCare Compact uses a separate pressurised tank for much higher steam output, worth it if you iron large piles regularly.

guide.q: Do I need an iron designed for hard water areas?
guide.a: If you live somewhere with hard water, a model like the Polti Vaporella here that works with plain tap water and has a clear descaling indicator saves the hassle of buying filtered or distilled water. Most other irons still work in hard water areas but may need more frequent descaling to avoid scale flecks appearing on clothes.

guide.q: How much does iron weight actually matter?
guide.a: A lighter iron like the Morphy Richards LightGlide here, at under 1kg, is genuinely easier on the arm during long ironing sessions and particularly helpful for anyone with mobility issues like arthritis. Heavier irons like the Philips Azur can use their own weight to help press out creases, so it's a trade-off between comfort and pressing power.

guide.q: How do I clean and descale a steam iron?
guide.a: Always unplug the iron and let it cool completely before cleaning, wiping the soleplate with a damp cloth and avoiding abrasive pads, vinegar or chemicals unless the manual specifically says to use them. Follow your model's specific descaling instructions, using only the water type it recommends, since methods vary between self-clean functions and removable scale collectors.
